subject: DPA role mapping + interstate data transfer controls (CPRA/CCPA)
messages:
From: Emily Rose <emily.rose@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA role mapping + interstate data transfer controls (CPRA/CCPA)

Hi Priya / Karthik —

Thanks for taking a look at our updated DPA (attached: ACME-DPA-v2.pdf). A few quick items the procurement team asked us to confirm before we can push this to legal: 

- We need explicit language confirming Redwood acts as a "Service Provider" under California law (CPRA) and that you will not "sell" personal information. Is your standard clause the typical "service provider/processor" flow-down?
- Subprocessor visibility: can you provide the current list of subprocessors and a description of categories of processing (telemetry, metrics, hosting, support)? We expect a CSV we can upload into our vendor system.
- Interstate transfers: ACME operates in multiple US states and some records will be processed in different data center regions. Are you able to commit to limiting export of California residents' personal data to non-California data centers without additional notice, or alternatively provide contractual controls (encryption in transit, KMS controls, access logs)?
- Audit evidence: SOC 2 timing and whether you can provide a copy of the latest SOC 2 Type II or a bridge letter.

Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the redlines? Preferably 10–11 AM PT.

Attachments: ACME-DPA-v2.pdf

Best,
Emily Rose
Senior Counsel, Privacy
ACME Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Rose <emily.rose@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA role mapping + interstate data transfer controls (CPRA/CCPA)

Emily —

Thanks for the clear list. Happy to run through this; 10:30 AM PT tomorrow works for me. For a quick start, answers inline below.

1) Service provider / sale language
We treat customer data as governed by the DPA and by default operate under a "service provider" model for the CPRA — we do not engage in "sales" of personal information. Our standard DPA uses the term "Service Provider (Processor)" and includes a flow-down requirement for subprocessors. We can add explicit CPRA-friendly language if that helps ACME's procurement checklist.

2) Subprocessor visibility
We maintain a maintained list and can export a CSV (we update it monthly). I will attach the current list to the thread prior to the call. As a practice, we notify customers 30 days before adding a subprocessor that impacts security or processing location; for lower-risk support tools we provide periodic disclosures.

3) Interstate transfers and regional controls
We do not currently offer a contractual guarantee to never process CA residents' data outside of CA data centers, but we can provide compensating technical and contractual controls: TLS in transit, customer-keyed KMS option (for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers get our managed KMS), strict role-based access controls, and per-request access logs with 90-day retention (longer on Dedicated). If ACME needs a strict CA-only processing guarantee, that would be an enterprise-only feature we can discuss as an amendment.

4) Audit evidence
We can provide our latest SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and have a SOC 2 bridge letter for the current quarter.

I'll circulate the subprocessor CSV (and a short note mapping common subprocessor categories to functions) before our call. Karthik — can you prepare suggested redline language for the CPRA-specific clauses (no sale, agents/service provider mapping, and transfer safeguards)?

Thanks — speak tomorrow.

—
Priya Natarajan
Senior Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Emily Rose <emily.rose@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA role mapping + interstate data transfer controls (CPRA/CCPA)

Emily / Priya —

Thanks — quick technical suggestions ahead of the call so we can focus on commercial points: 

- Recommended clause text (short): 
  "For purposes of the CPRA and analogous state privacy laws, Vendor is a Service Provider (Processor) and will not Sell personal information. Vendor will process Personal Information only on Customer's documented instructions and shall implement and maintain reasonable administrative, physical, and technical safeguards as described in Schedule A."

- Subprocessors: we will attach Redwood-SP-list-June2026.csv. It includes categories: cloud infra (GCP us-west/us-east), metrics & telemetry (Datadog, internal anonymizer), auth & SSO (Okta), email & support (Zendesk). We can mark which subprocessors process CA data and which are US-only.

- Transfers / controls: operationally, we use regional routing for low-latency inference; the runtime may serve requests from the nearest region. For customers requiring stricter control, we offer two options: (a) pinning to a region via Dedicated/Private deployments, or (b) envelope encryption with customer-managed keys so even if computation occurs in another region, plaintext is not accessible without key access. Recommend offering template contract language that says: "Vendor will implement encryption in transit and provide access logs; for encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, Vendor will not have access to key material."

- Audit evidence: SOC 2 available under NDA; additionally, we can provide an extract showing relevant control mappings to CPRA sections on request.

I will draft a short redline for the CPRA no-sale + subprocessor notice provisions and drop it into the shared drive before the call.

- Karthik
